subject: Exec approval request: FinThrive competitive protections
messages:
From: Dan Murphy <dan.murphy@finthrive.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Commercial protections request (MFN / benchmark / exclusivity)

Connor — thanks for the demo last week. FinThrive is excited about Redwood's latency profile and the prospect of moving our recommendations pipeline onto your Dedicated tier. Before we proceed to procurement, a couple of commercial asks came up from our board: 

- MFN: request that Redwood provide MFN on per-unit pricing vs any public or enterprise offer for the next 12 months.
- Benchmark guarantee: if P95 latency for the production model exceeds 200ms over a rolling 30-day window, we get a fee credit tied to SLA.
- Exclusivity: a 6-month exclusivity in our vertical (digital wealth advisors) while we pilot.

We understand some of these are non-standard; happy to discuss constraining language. Attached is an expanded RFP and some sample commercial language. Can you run this with your commercial/legal team and share a path to signoff? We're targeting a commitment by mid-October.

Attachments: FinThrive_RFP_attachments.pdf

Best —
Dan
Dan Murphy
Head of Partnerships, FinThrive

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dan Murphy <dan.murphy@finthrive.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Commercial protections request (MFN / benchmark / exclusivity)

Dan — thanks for this and for the clear asks. High level I think there's forward motion but we need to narrow the scope to reduce precedent risk and operational ambiguity. A few early thoughts: 

- MFN: willing to consider a "pricing parity" commitment for identical contracted product bundles and committed volumes only (exclude trials, promotional credits, and partner reseller offers). Timebox to 12 months and include notice periods for legitimately lower prices.
- Benchmark/SLA credit: ok in principle but need to clearly define the metric (model variant, sequence length distribution) and exclude customer-caused degradations. Also prefer credits tied to monthly usage rather than open-ended damages.
- Exclusivity: 6 months is material; likely we can offer a non-solicitation / preferred supplier commitment instead of absolute exclusivity.

Looping in Marissa and Laura for pricing & commercial impact. I'll start a formal redline and share a proposed concession set.

Connor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(concession_redlines.docx attached)

Subject: Escalation: FinThrive requests MFN + benchmark + 6mo exclusivity — needs exec signoff

Team — I'm escalating this to Deal Desk / Legal / Sales Leadership. FinThrive (high-value pilot, expected $1.2M ARR on-year-two) is asking for three high-risk items: 12-month MFN, an operationally-tight benchmark credit, and a 6-month vertical exclusivity. 

Why this needs executive review:
- MFN establishes precedent across enterprise deals — limits future pricing flexibility across similar verticals.
- Benchmark credit is acceptable in principle but the measurement window and model scope are ambiguous — could trigger frequent credits.
- Exclusivity materially restricts our go-to-market in wealth vertical; we need to understand compensation and partner impact.

Immediate asks: 
1) Legal (Rishi): provide a short memo on risk and an alternative clause (we need contract language we can present).
2) Pricing/Deal Desk (Laura): quantify revenue delta at 10/15/20% capped discounts and list any mandatory concessions for granting exclusivity.
3) Sales Leadership (Markus): recommend whether to pursue pilot under these terms or push back.

Attached: MAL-DealSummary.pdf (includes ARR estimate, retention assumptions, suggested concession matrix). Need direction by EOD tomorrow to hit FinThrive's procurement timeline.

— Marissa
VP, Sales Operations

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation: FinThrive requests MFN + benchmark + 6mo exclusivity — needs exec signoff

Quick legal take — high level risks and suggested language below. Will need final review, but this buys clarity for commercial decisioning: 

Risks:
- Broad MFN referencing "any public or enterprise offer" is too open-ended; it ties our hands on promotions and partner pricing. Precedent risk if we accept unqualified MFNs.
- Benchmark SLA without narrow metric definitions and exclusions (customer abuse, data skew, model updates) invites credits that scale unpredictably.
- Exclusivity across a vertical is a go-to-market restriction; could trigger competitive escalation from partners and limit future marketplace listings.

Suggested alternatives (sample clause snippets):
1) Limited MFN: "For a period of twelve (12) months following Effective Date, Redwood will not intentionally offer a lower per-unit price for the same product bundle and committed monthly volume to any third party in the digital wealth advisors vertical. Exclusions: promotional trials, partner reseller pricing, and short-term promotional discounts less than thirty (30) days. Redwood reserves the right to reduce prices for legal/regulatory reasons or errors."

2) Benchmark credit (defined): "Benchmark measurement will use the agreed model variant (mm-v2) on production traffic excluding test and backfill jobs. If monthly P95 inference latency exceeds 200ms for two (2) consecutive calendar months attributable to Redwood's infrastructure, Customer will receive a credit equal to 10% of that month's hosting fees, subject to a cap of 3% of annual fees. Credits will not apply where latency degradation is due to Customer workload patterns, misuse, or unsupported model changes."

3) Exclusivity alternative: "Customer receives a six (6) month 'preferred supplier' right of first negotiation for projects in the digital wealth advisors vertical; this is not an exclusivity covenant and does not prevent Redwood from serving other customers in the vertical. Any exclusivity request must be accompanied by a mutually agreed financial premium and a non-refundable commitment fee."

I'll put these snippets into a short memo and mark the clauses as high/medium/low risk. If leadership wants to move forward, we should condition any MFN on a minimum committed volume and a maximum discount cap.

Rishi
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
(legal_clauses_suggestion.txt attached)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec decision request — recommended concessions for FinThrive pilot (urgent)

Marissa / Markus — below is a concise recommendation and the ask for exec signoff so we can respond to FinThrive by tomorrow morning. I've summarized commercial impact (see attached MAL-DealSummary).

Recommendation (reasoned compromise):
- MFN: accept a Limited MFN (Rishi language) limited to identical product bundles and committed volumes; timebox 12 months; exclude promotions/trials; require a minimum 6-month committed spend of $150k.
- Benchmark SLA: accept defined P95 latency credit with the 10% monthly hosting credit and a ceiling equal to 3% of annual fees; exclude customer-caused degradation; tie measurement to agreed model variant and telemetry.
- Exclusivity: decline absolute exclusivity. Offer a 6-month Preferred Supplier commitment with a $25k non-refundable onboarding premium and right of first negotiation for new projects (Rishi language).
- Pricing: cap total recurring discount impact at 20% for the pilot. Any deeper discount requires CFO/CRO signoff.

Why: this preserves the deal while limiting precedent and financial exposure. The MFN is narrowed and conditional; the benchmark credit is bounded; exclusivity converted to a commercial premium.

Requested action: please approve the package below or provide edits. If approved, I'll send the proposed redline to Dan and attach Rishi's suggested language. Need a thumbs-up by EOD tonight to meet procurement timing.

Proposed next message to FinThrive (one-liner): "We can accept a timeboxed, limited MFN and a defined benchmark credit under the attached terms; exclusivity is not possible but we will provide a Preferred Supplier commitment with a premium. Please confirm acceptance and we'll circulate a redline."

Connor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: MAL-DealSummary.pdf
